title: Clausulae Characteristicae
subtitle: Nemo est qui hoc credat — clausula relativa describens genus, non factum specificum.
objectives: Distinguere clausulam relativam factualem (indicativus) a characteristica (coniunctivus)
Identificare antecedentes typici quae signalant clausulam characteristicam (nemo, solus, unus, dignus)
Vertere clausulam characteristicam correcte: 'the sort/kind of person who...'
Formare clausulas characteristicas cum consecutione temporum apta

content.intro: Compara: Vir quī vēnit meus amīcus est. ('The man who came is my friend' — factum specificum, indicativus) vs. Nēmō est quī hoc crēdat. ('There is no one WHO WOULD believe this' — genus/characteristica, coniunctivus).
content.explanation: Clausula relātīva charactēristica dēscrībit nōn factum ūnicum, sed TYPUM vel GENUS ('the sort of person who...'). Antecēdēns est frequenter indēfīnītus, negātīvus, vel superlātīvus.

rules.heading: a) Antecedentes Typici
rules.body: nēmō (no one), nūllus (none), sōlus/ūnus (only/one who), dignus/indignus (worthy/unworthy), sunt quī ('there are those who' — indēfīnītum), quis est quī ('who is there who...').

rules.heading: b) Constructio: Qui/Quae/Quod + Coniunctivus
rules.body: Sunt quī hoc crēdant. ('There are those WHO BELIEVE this [as a type].') Nihil est quod nōn possit vincere labor. ('There is nothing THAT hard work cannot conquer' — Vergilius, adaptātum.)

rules.heading: c) Dignus/Indignus + Qui + Coniunctivus
rules.body: Cōnstrūctiō speciālis frequēns: Dignus est quī laudētur. ('He is worthy TO BE PRAISED', litt. 'worthy who should be praised'.)

rules.heading: d) Distinctio: Factuale vs. Characteristica
rules.body:
FactualisCharacteristica
Modusindicativusconiunctivus
Significatiofact specifictype/kind/sort
ExemplumVir quī vēnit... (the man who came)Nēmō est quī crēdat... (no one of the sort who believes)

examples: Nemo est qui te non amet. — There is no one who does not love you.
Solus est qui hoc facere possit. — He is the only one who can do this.
Sunt qui haec vera esse credant. — There are those who believe these things to be true.
Dignus est qui memoria teneatur. — He is worthy to be remembered.
Quis est tam stultus qui hoc non videat? — Who is so foolish as not to see this?

commonMistakes.wrong: Clausula relativa post 'nemo'/'solus' tractatur ut factualis, cum indicativo.
commonMistakes.right: Post antecedentes indefinitos/negativos/superlativos (nemo, solus, sunt qui...), clausula relativa est characteristica: coniunctivus.
commonMistakes.why: Antecedens ipse est indicium fortis quod clausula describit typum, non factum specificum unum.

commonMistakes.wrong: 'Dignus qui laudetur' vertitur litteraliter 'worthy who is praised', confusum grammaticaliter.
commonMistakes.right: Melius vertitur idiomaticē: 'worthy TO BE praised' — constructio fixa cum dignus/indignus.
commonMistakes.why: Traductio litteralis interdum non capit sensum idiomaticum constructionis Latinae.

items.prompt: 'Nemo est qui hoc credat' est clausula:
'Vir quī vēnit meus amīcus est' — 'vēnit' est:
Quod antecedens frequenter signalat clausulam characteristicam?
Solus est qui hoc facere ___. (can — possit)
Dignus est qui ___. (be remembered — memoria teneatur)

summary: Clausula relativa characteristica: qui/quae/quod + coniunctivus, describens genus, non factum.
Antecedentes typici: nemo, solus, unus, sunt qui, dignus/indignus.
Contrasta cum clausula relativa factuale (indicativus, Gradus III).
